# Sloc Cloc and Code (scc)

![SCC illustration](./scc.jpg)

A tool similar to cloc, sloccount and tokei. For counting the lines of code, blank lines, comment lines, and physical lines of source code in many programming languages.

Goal is to be the fastest code counter possible, but also perform COCOMO calculation like sloccount, LOCOMO estimation for LLM-based development costs, estimate code complexity similar to cyclomatic complexity calculators and produce unique lines of code or DRYness metrics. In short one tool to rule them all.

Also it has a very short name which is easy to type `scc`.

If you don't like sloc cloc and code feel free to use the name `Succinct Code Counter`.

Licensed under MIT licence.

## Install

### Snap

A snap install exists.

`$ sudo snap install scc`

*NB* Snap installed applications cannot run outside of `/home` so you may encounter issues if you use snap and attempt to run outside this directory.

### Homebrew

Or if you have Homebrew installed

`$ brew install scc`

### Fedora

Fedora Linux users can use a COPR repository:

`$ sudo dnf copr enable lihaohong/scc && sudo dnf install scc`

### MacPorts

On macOS, you can also install via MacPorts

`$ sudo port install scc`

### Scoop

Or if you are using Scoop on Windows

`$ scoop install scc`

### Chocolatey

Or if you are using Chocolatey on Windows

`$ choco install scc`

### WinGet

Or if you are using WinGet on Windows

`winget install --id benboyter.scc --source winget`

### FreeBSD

On FreeBSD, scc is available as a package

`$ pkg install scc`

Or, if you prefer to build from source, you can use the ports tree

`$ cd /usr/ports/devel/scc && make install clean`

### Run in Docker

Go to the directory you want to run scc from.

Run the command below to run the latest release of scc on your current working directory:

```bash
docker run --rm -it -v "$PWD:/pwd"  ghcr.io/boyter/scc:master scc /pwd
```

### Manual

Binaries for Windows, GNU/Linux and macOS for both i386 and x86_64 machines are available from the releases page.

## Usage

Command line usage of `scc` is designed to be as simple as possible.
Full details can be found in `scc --help` or `scc -h`.

```text
Sloc, Cloc and Code. Count lines of code in a directory with complexity estimation.

Usage:
  scc [flags] [files or directories]

Flags:
      --avg-wage int                       average wage value used for basic COCOMO calculation (default 56286)
      --binary                             disable binary file detection
      --by-file                            display output for every file
  -m, --character                          calculate max and mean characters per line
      --ci                                 enable CI output settings where stdout is ASCII
      --cocomo-project-type string         change COCOMO model type [organic, semi-detached, embedded, "custom,1,1,1,1"] (default "organic")
      --count-as string                    count extension as language [e.g. jsp:htm,chead:"C Header" maps extension jsp to html and chead to C Header]
      --count-ignore                       set to allow .gitignore and .ignore files to be counted
      --currency-symbol string             set currency symbol (default "$")
      --debug                              enable debug output
      --directory-walker-job-workers int   controls the maximum number of workers which will walk the directory tree (default 8)
  -a, --dryness                            calculate the DRYness of the project (implies --uloc)
      --eaf float                          the effort adjustment factor derived from the cost drivers (1.0 if rated nominal) (default 1)
      --exclude-dir strings                directories to exclude (default [.git,.hg,.svn])

## Unique Lines of Code (ULOC)

ULOC can be used to determine how many DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) code you have. It provides a measurement of unique lines of code.

To get ULOC output use the `--uloc` flag or `-u`:

```text
$ scc --uloc .
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Language                 Files     Lines   Blanks  Comments     Code Complexity    ULOC
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Go                          13     7,340      896       455    5,989      1,076   4,456
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

To calculate DRYness percentage use the `--dryness` flag or `-a`:

```text
$ scc --dryness .
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Language                 Files     Lines   Blanks  Comments     Code Complexity    DRYness
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Go                          13     7,340      896       455    5,989      1,076       74.4%
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

## COCOMO

COCOMO (Constructive Cost Model) calculates the estimated cost to build the code. scc uses the basic COCOMO model to provide estimates.

The COCOMO calculation is always run and will appear at the bottom of the output unless you use `--no-cocomo`.

Example:

```text
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Estimated Cost to Develop (organic) $12,517,562
Estimated Schedule Effort (organic) 35.93 months
Estimated People Required (organic) 30.95
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

You can customize COCOMO calculation with:

- `--avg-wage` - Set the average wage (default 56286)
- `--cocomo-project-type` - Change COCOMO model type: organic, semi-detached, embedded (default "organic")
- `--eaf` - Effort adjustment factor (default 1.0)
- `--currency-symbol` - Set currency symbol (default "$")

## LOCOMO

LOCOMO is an extension of COCOMO for calculating costs when using LLM (Large Language Model) based development approaches. It estimates token counts, API costs, and developer time when using AI assistants.

This is an experimental feature for estimating costs when using AI-powered development tools.

## Output Formats

scc supports multiple output formats for integration with other tools:

- `tabular` (default) - Human-readable table format
- `wide` - Wider table with additional statistics
- `json` - JSON format for programmatic processing
- `json2` - Alternative JSON format
- `csv` - CSV format
- `csv-stream` - Streaming CSV format
- `cloc-yaml` - YAML format compatible with cloc
- `html` - HTML report
- `html-table` - HTML table only
- `sql` - SQL CREATE and INSERT statements
- `sql-insert` - SQL INSERT statements only
- `openmetrics` - OpenMetrics/Prometheus format

Example:

```bash
scc --format json .
scc --format csv --output report.csv .
```

## Ignore Files

`scc` supports .ignore files inside directories that it scans. # Sloc Cloc and Code (scc)

![SCC illustration](./scc.jpg)

A tool similar to cloc, sloccount and tokei. For counting the lines of code, blank lines, comment lines, and physical lines of source code in many programming languages.

Goal is to be the fastest code counter possible, but also perform COCOMO calculation like sloccount, LOCOMO estimation for LLM-based development costs, estimate code complexity similar to cyclomatic complexity calculators and produce unique lines of code or DRYness metrics. In short one tool to rule them all.

Also it has a very short name which is easy to type `scc`.

If you don't like sloc cloc and code feel free to use the name `Succinct Code Counter`.

Licensed under MIT licence.

## Install

### Snap

A snap install exists.

`$ sudo snap install scc`

*NB* Snap installed applications cannot run outside of `/home` so you may encounter issues if you use snap and attempt to run outside this directory.

### Homebrew

Or if you have Homebrew installed

`$ brew install scc`

### Fedora

Fedora Linux users can use a COPR repository:

`$ sudo dnf copr enable lihaohong/scc && sudo dnf install scc`

### MacPorts

On macOS, you can also install via MacPorts

`$ sudo port install scc`

### Scoop

Or if you are using Scoop on Windows

`$ scoop install scc`

### Chocolatey

Or if you are using Chocolatey on Windows

`$ choco install scc`

### WinGet

Or if you are using WinGet on Windows

`winget install --id benboyter.scc --source winget`

### FreeBSD

On FreeBSD, scc is available as a package

`$ pkg install scc`

Or, if you prefer to build from source, you can use the ports tree

`$ cd /usr/ports/devel/scc && make install clean`

### Run in Docker

Go to the directory you want to run scc from.

Run the command below to run the latest release of scc on your current working directory:

```bash
docker run --rm -it -v "$PWD:/pwd"  ghcr.io/boyter/scc:master scc /pwd
```

Binaries for Windows, GNU/Linux and macOS for both i386 and x86_64 machines are available from the releases page.

```

Language                 Files     Lines   Blanks  Comments     Code Complexity    DRYness
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Go                          13     7,340      896       455    5,989      1,076       74.4%
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

Estimated Schedule Effort (organic) 35.93 months

def go_str_slice_slice(items):

def go_str_slice(items):
    if not items:
        return "nil"
    quoted = [f'"{item}"' for item in items]
    return "{" + ", ".join(quoted) + "}"

def go_str_slice_slice(items):
    if not items:
        return "nil"
    inner = []
    for pair in items:
        inner.append("{" + ", ".join(f'"{x}"' for x in pair) + "}")
    return "{" + ", ".join(inner) + "}"

    lines.append(f'\t{{')

    lines.append(f'\t\tExtensions:       {go_str_slice(exts)},')
    lines.append(f'\t\tLineComment:      {go_str_slice(line_comments)},')
    lines.append(f'\t\tMultiLineComment: {go_str_slice_slice(multiline)},')
    lines.append(f'\t\tComplexityChecks: {go_str_slice(complexity)},')
    lines.append(f'\t}},')

lines.append("}")

output = "\n".join(lines)
with open("/workspace/languages.go", "w") as f:

def go_str_slice(items):
    if not items:
        return "nil"
    quoted = ['"{}"'.format(item.replace('\\', '\\\\').replace('"', '\\"')) for item in items]
    return "[]string{" + ", ".join(quoted) + "}"

def go_str_slice_slice(items):
    if not items:
        return "nil"
    inner = []
    for pair in items:
        inner_items = ['"{}"'.format(x.replace('\\', '\\\\').replace('"', '\\"')) for x in pair]
        inner.append("[]string{" + ", ".join(inner_items) + "}")
    return "[][]string{" + ", ".join(inner) + "}"

def go_str_slice_slice(items):
    if not items:
        return "nil"
    inner = []
    for pair in items:
        inner_items = ['"{}"'.format(x.replace('\\', '\\\\').replace('"', '\\"')) for x in pair]
        inner.append("[]string{" + ", ".join(inner_items) + "}")
    return "[][]string{" + ", ".join(inner) + "}"

def go_str_slice(items):
    if not items:
        return "nil"
    quoted = ['"{}"'.format(item.replace('\\', '\\\\').replace('"', '\\"')) for item in items]
    return "[]string{" + ", ".join(quoted) + "}"

def go_str_slice_slice(items):
    if not items:
        return "nil"
    inner = []
    for pair in items:
        inner_items = ['"{}"'.format(x.replace('\\', '\\\\').replace('"', '\\"')) for x in pair]
        inner.append("[]string{" + ", ".join(inner_items) + "}")
    return "[][]string{" + ", ".join(inner) + "}"

# Wide format exact analysis
header = 'Language                              Files     Lines   Blanks  Comments     Code Complexity Complexity/Lines'
data   = 'Go                                        1         9        2         2        5          0             0.00'

words_pos = []
pos = 0
for word in ['Language', 'Files', 'Lines', 'Blanks', 'Comments', 'Code', 'Complexity', 'Complexity/Lines']:
    idx = header.find(word, pos)
    if idx >= 0:
        words_pos.append((idx, idx+len(word)-1, word))

    print(f'{word}: [{start}:{end}]')
print()

# Language: 0-37 = 38 chars (left-aligned)
# Files ends at: 42 = 38+5-1
# Lines ends at: 52 = 43+?
# etc.
prev = 0
for start, end, word in words_pos:
    field_data = data[prev:end+1]
    print(f'{word}: [{prev}:{end+1}] = {repr(field_data.rstrip())} (end={end})')
    prev = end + 1
EOF

# Key differences in by-file output:
# 1. Original format: 
#    - Language row (Go header)
#    - border
#    - file rows for Go
#    - border 
#    - Language row (Python header)
#    - border
#    - file rows for Python
#    - border

# My format:
#    - All language rows first (Go, Python)
#    - border
#    - file rows for Go
#    - border
#    - file rows for Python
#    - border

# The original interleaves language headers with their file rows!
# And the language header comes BEFORE the border, then files, then border

# Also: COCOMO $919 vs $920 issue remains

# The by-file format requires a different structure:
# For each language in sorted order:
#   1. Print language header row (same as non-by-file)
#   2. Print border
#   3. Print each file row
#   4. Print border (after all files of this language)

# Wait looking at original more carefully:
# Go row (with files count) -> border -> file rows -> border ->
# Python row -> border -> file rows -> border -> Total -> border -> ...

# So the language rows appear INTERSPERSED with file rows!
# And the structure is:
# header border -> [for each lang: lang_row -> border -> file_rows -> border] -> total -> ...

print("Original by-file structure:")
print("header")
print("border")
print("[for each language:")
print("  language_row")
print("  border")
print("  file_rows...")
print("  border")
print("]")
print("Total")
print("...")
EOF

# '12' at positions 35-36 (right edge at 36) = Lines column right edge ✓
# Line ends at 36 (no more data after Complexity/Lines columns)

# So the char row format is:
# 'MaxLine / MeanLine' (label, 18 chars) + spaces to fill to 20 (lang col)
# + right-align Max at Files position (24)
# + right-align Mean at Lines position (36)
# Then NOTHING else (no Blanks, Comments, Code, Complexity)

# The label 'MaxLine / MeanLine' is NOT truncated! (18 < 20 chars)

# My issue:
# 1. I put Max at charVals[4] (Code col) and Mean at charVals[5] (Complexity col)
#    But it should be: Max at charVals[0] (Files col) and Mean at charVals[1] (Lines col)!
# 2. The 20-char lang name truncation is applied to the label too
#    But 'MaxLine / MeanLine' (18 chars) should NOT be truncated

# For issue 2: the formatLanguageName function uses truncation at 15 display width
# 'MaxLine / MeanLine' = 18 chars > 15 -> gets truncated to 14+1=15!
# That's WRONG for these special labels

# The special labels ('MaxLine / MeanLine', '(ULOC)', 'Total', 'Percentage', etc.)
# should NOT be truncated - they should be padded to 20 with spaces
# OR: the truncation only applies to actual language names?

# Looking at original: 'MaxLine / MeanLine' (18 chars) -> NOT truncated even though > 15
# 'Unique Lines of Code (ULOC)' (26 chars) -> shown as 'Unique Lines of Code (ULOC)'
# in a 20-char column!

# So special rows DON'T use truncation at 15!

# 52.7% at [32:37] -> Lines column, right-aligns to 36 ✓

# 22.2% at [52:57] -> Comments column, right-aligns to 56 ✓
# 60.0% at [64:69] -> Code column... right-aligns to 68? (not 67!)
# 41.7% at [75:80] -> Complexity column, right-aligns to 79 (not 78!)

# The normal right-edge positions are: Files=24, Lines=36, Blanks=46, Comments=56, Code=67, Complexity=78
# But percent row puts: Files=24, Lines=36, Blanks=46, Comments=56, Code=68!, Complexity=79!

# That's 1 wider for Code and Complexity!
# Code: normally 4-char value + 1 space = 5 chars (right-edge 67)
# But percent: 5-char value + 1 space = 6 chars (right-edge 68)

# The percent row uses WIDER fields for Code and Complexity!
# Because '60.0%' and '41.7%' are 5 chars, need to fit in the Code field without trimming

# The Code column format is '%4s %10s' = 4 chars + 1 space + 10 chars
# For percent values: '60.0%' = 5 chars. In '%4s' it would truncate! No, %4s just prints 5 chars.
# So '%4s' of '60.0%' = '60.0%' (5 chars, no padding needed since >4)

# Test: what does my format string produce for percent values?
fmt = '%-20s%5s       %5s    %6s  %8s       %4s %10s'

expected = 'Percentage          50.0%       52.7%     50.0%     22.2%       60.0%      41.7%'

EOF

func makePercentVals(all []*LanguageSummary, s *LanguageSummary, isWide bool, showULOC bool, showDryness bool) []string {
	var totFiles, totLines, totBlanks, totComments, totCode, totComplexity int64
	for _, ls := range all {
		totFiles += ls.Count
		totLines += ls.Lines
		totBlanks += ls.Blank
		totComments += ls.Comment
		totCode += ls.Code
		totComplexity += ls.Complexity
	}

	pct := func(part, total int64) string {
		if total == 0 {
			return "NaN%"
		}
		return fmt.Sprintf("%.1f%%", float64(part)/float64(total)*100)
	}

	vals := []string{
		pct(s.Count, totFiles),
		pct(s.Lines, totLines),
		pct(s.Blank, totBlanks),
		pct(s.Comment, totComments),
		pct(s.Code, totCode),
		pct(s.Complexity, totComplexity),
	}
	if isWide {
		vals = append(vals, "") // Complexity/Lines %
	}
	if showULOC && !showDryness {
		vals = append(vals, "") // ULOC %
	} else if showDryness {
		vals = append(vals, "") // Dryness %
	}
	return vals
}

func makeSeparator(width int, opts *Options) string {
	if opts.CI {
		return strings.Repeat("-", width)
	}
	return strings.Repeat("-", width)

# Normal percent row positions (right-edges): Files=24, Lines=36, Blanks=46, Comments=56, Code=67, Complexity=78

def make_pct_row(label, values, total_width=79):
    """values = (files%, lines%, blanks%, comments%, code%, complexity%)"""
    positions = [24, 36, 46, 56, 67, 78]
    buf = list(' ' * total_width)
    
    # Place label (left-aligned in lang col, max 20 chars)
    label_display = label[:20]  # NO TRUNCATION for labels
    for i, c in enumerate(label_display):
        buf[i] = c
    
    # Place each value at fixed position
    for pos, val in zip(positions, values):
        val_str = str(val)
        start = pos - len(val_str) + 1
        if start < 0:
            start = 0
        for i, c in enumerate(val_str):
            if 0 <= start+i < total_width:
                buf[start+i] = c
    
    # Trim trailing spaces
    return ''.join(buf).rstrip()

# Test:

print('Test:    ', repr(test))
print('Expected:', repr(expected))
print('Match:', test == expected)
EOF

# The LanguageSummary struct has WeightedComplexity float64

# (when files are available) OR store it in a non-JSON field

# The original exports WeightedComplexity=0, so I should match

old_agg = '\t\ts.WeightedComplexity += r.WeightedComplexity'
new_agg = '\t\ts.ComplexityRatio += r.WeightedComplexity'

content = content.replace(old_agg, new_agg, 1)

with open('/workspace/formatter.go', 'w') as f:
    f.write(content)
print("Updated LanguageSummary struct")
EOF

# The ignore files that should NOT be counted by default:
# .gitignore, .ignore, .sccignore, .dockerignore, .hgignore, etc.

# These are the "ignore files" that scc uses for its own patterns
# When --count-ignore is set, they ARE counted

# In processor.go walkDir, I need to add a check:
# If the file is an ignore file AND !opts.CountIgnore: skip it

# The ignore files are: .gitignore, .ignore, .sccignore, .gitmodule patterns

# But actually looking at the actual behavior more carefully:
# The .gitignore file is being ignored from scanning (only .log is skipped)
# Maybe the issue is that my code is also processing .gitignore as a language file?

# The .gitignore has extension '.gitignore' which maps to the 'gitignore' language!
# And with --count-ignore disabled, these should be skipped

# Actually: looking at the scc behavior: it doesn't count .gitignore etc by default
# This is done by skipping these files when walking the directory

# The current file walker should skip these files but apparently doesn't

# Fix: in the walker, skip ignore files unless --count-ignore is set

with open('/workspace/processor.go', 'r') as f:
    content = f.read()

# Add ignore file check in walkDir
old = '''		if isExcludedFile(name, opts) {
\t\t\tcontinue
\t\t}'''

new = '''		if isExcludedFile(name, opts) {
\t\t\tcontinue
\t\t}

\t\t// Skip ignore files unless --count-ignore is set
\t\tif !opts.CountIgnore && isIgnoreFile(name) {
\t\t\tcontinue
\t\t}'''

content = content.replace(old, new, 1)

with open('/workspace/processor.go', 'w') as f:
    f.write(content)
print("Updated walkDir to skip ignore files")
EOF
